description:
Somos Mission Control 7, una tripulación multidisciplinaria de Tegucigalpa enfocada en fusionar (IoT), la Inteligencia Artificial y el modelado científico. Nuestro objetivo es transformar los datos satelitales de la NASA en soluciones AgTech tangibles para el desafío Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

No solo escribimos código; construimos arquitecturas híbridas donde el hardware físico local y la telemetría espacial trabajan juntos para proteger la próxima frontera de la agricultura.
summary: We developed Agro Stellar, a smart agriculture platform that integrates historical satellite data with a physical monitoring rover. To address the challenge of climate variability in agricultural production, the system combines 20 years of climate records from the NASA POWER API (2006–2025) with real-time telemetry captured by soil moisture sensors (HL-69) and microclimate sensors (BME680) onboard an ESP32, along with computer vision using NASA and Google APIs, and voice synthesis to diagnose crop health instantly. This project matters because it bridges the gap between macro-scale space data and the specific reality of each plot, enabling farmers to optimize irrigation, reduce losses in essential crops such as beans and corn, and make agricultural decisions grounded in accessible science.
details: Agro Stellar is a smart agriculture platform that bridges the gap between macro-scale satellite data and the reality of each plot through a three-stage system: it analyzes 20 years of NASA climate history (2006–2025), validates real-time ground conditions with an exploration rover, and projects the yield of local crops such as beans and corn over a 3- to 6-month horizon. Built with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, C++, and Firebase Realtime Database, and deployed on Vercel, the project integrates the NASA POWER API with a low-cost physical prototype powered by an ESP32, Bluetooth control (Dabble), an L298N motor driver, a wireless optical camera, and BME680 and HL-69 sensors that transmit temperature, ambient humidity, pressure, VOC gases, and soil moisture in real time. Its main innovation lies in incorporating Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (TTS) as an agronomic copilot capable of observing the crop and auditing the sensors to provide diagnoses, optimizing water use and democratizing space science for Honduran farmers under three criteria: low cost, easy interpretation, and lightweight connectivity for rural areas.
